I just read the thread about "approved reddit mods" coming over to voat. It made me furious. Here we are, moving to voat to get away from these power-hungry basement trolls just to find that they have already established themselves here.

I realize we cant stop them from participating in this community, but I think its necessary to prevent them or any other single person from having too much influence over this community.

This could be done by severely limiting the total number of subs one IP can moderate. Maybe even classify it by subscribers, so you can be the mod of one sub with a lot of subscribers, or many subs with few subscribers. That way no one person will have a significant impact on the community.

Further, and more importantly, we should figure out some way to prevent any mods from censoring content. The whole reason why we are here is to get away from the overbearing rules and censorship on reddit. The last thing we want is for this place to turn into a wasteland too. Obviously mods need the ability to delete shit posts, but there should be a high level of transparency combined with actual consequences for unnecessarily censoring content. I have no idea how this would be implemented, but I think its important to preserve the integrity of the community.
Set a limit to the number of subs one person can mod and track it by IP. Also set controls to prevent mods from censoring content.

The amount of subverses you can moderate has already been limited by username and (I think) a measure to limit it on the basis of an IP is being worked on.

On the censorship part there have been some popular posts about how, amongst other things, there should be a log where such acts are posted. Pretty much everything you are worrying about is already on the list of priorities of a very small team of developers.

/u/Johnparish' comment below mine is superior, upvote that instead.

I have heard this and two things, IP tracking is useless for anyone who wants to gets around it, and 2, IP tracking unfairly hurts groups, and roommates, communities unfairly.

Also, three things that we as a collective have is 1, only 10 sub modded per account. You would need to manage 40 accounts to get to that magic 400 that one guy mods. 2, you have to be active or you can lose your modship if people want that sub. 3, public modlog, if we think something is fishy, it is right there in the mod log. Very helpful in weeding out those bad subverses we should avoid

Not perfect, but I do think it will help, at least a little bit.

Family Joining ceremony, Ruthga Home world. Earth year 2367

Listen here young ones and I’ll tell you of how we fight now and how we fought then. Back then we thought we knew how to fight, we believed ourselves masters of battle. The club, blades and melee weapons, all cast aside now; relics of the past.

I opened my paws into a circle shape and indicated my sires and the other young ones sit around.

Great battles we waged between tribes and villages, hacking, bashing and slicing each other to death and into cripples, and for what? We’d rush headlong into the fray, swinging wildly with our home made weapons and into the bodies, paws and heads of who we thought our enemies were – for hundreds of cycles we did this. Nothing changing. No real winners, just losers. Each warrior fighting for his own glory, out to get the highest kill count. Fathers destroyed leaving the young ones without a protector. Sons cut down before they could sire in a bloody mess for no net gain. Fighting for the sake of fighting is a noble cause but we always wanted more but didn’t know how.

We truly thought we knew how to fight, how to do battle. You understand this was how it was done. We sang songs about the great victories, the battles of the past…but not of the dead. No one sang songs of the dead.

Then they arrived. The Humans. We saw their ships and readied to fight them, in our traditional way. They stopped us. Stopped all of us, all the villages and tribes, each father and son, stopped us in less than (1 hour) with a cloud of coughing white they dropped from the ships. I now know they call this ‘tear gas’. Cubs, you can’t imagine how much I cursed them for that, for refusing to meet us on the fields like warriors. When we found what they wanted, my attitude changed. They wanted to train us, train us to fight as they fought. You’ve seen them, you know we’re stronger, but they’re faster and they’re tall while we are long. A good opponent and challenge. A good battle for a fine Ruthga warrior. But they had things they called ‘rules’ – not our one unspoken tradition of ‘don’t attack the females and new-borns’ but rule after rule after rule.

They trained us hard, we got hurt but they patched us up with medicine and sent us back to train. There was no let up in the training regimen. But we adapted, learned their ‘rules’ and I could see the changes in us; we became faster, more adaptable and more in tune with each other – anticipating each others moves before they make them. They taught us that should one of us fall, his team would look after him and the doctors would patch him up.

They gave us uniforms and divided us up into squads. We kept training, drilling and practicing…ever more keen for the fight. We trained against each other, then finally against the humans. They humiliated us, drove us into the mud, broken and bleeding with their teamwork. They trained us even harder after that.

The battles of our home world were forgotten, we had no time or energy left to carry out our own private struggles. We all could see the humans way of fighting was better. We got hurt less and less and if we did, they fixed us, not left us to die in the dirt as we had done. Petty rivalry between squads was encouraged by them, they arranged more and more squad on squad battles, all the while watching us. This was a better way to fight. Organised. Arranged. Hatred directed at the foe, not who should be our brothers. Watching out for each other, covering each others backs and flanks.

After (6 months) they saw fit to tell us we were ready. They took the best of us, a mere 15 warriors with a few in reserve to fight in the ‘6 planets’ - a supposedly legendary fight between 6 different races to determine the winner, the top warriors. I was one of those picked. Cubs chased after me in the street to catch a glimpse of me, the women…well, lets say I did well when I wore my uniform to and from the training camps.

After a long journey to the Humans home world for the fight, we didn’t know what to expect but we felt ready. How many of us - if any – would come back again we didn’t know. I looked at the faces around me…not one had I known before the Humans arrived, each face I would have happily swung a club into back then. Now I trusted them completely and they I.

We disembarked on landing and, written in our language and in several others was a sign welcoming us ‘1st Interplanetary Rugby Tournament’

We knew we’d have the greatest battle of our history ahead of us. We didn’t win the battle that year. Nor the next year, nor yet in fact. We’re the strongest in the fight but our ball transfer skills let us down. Now let’s go outside and practice our rear passes.
(OC) Humans taught us how to fight

Here's a rough outline of the current order of events relating to the development of the Civil Voaters' Agreement. This is subject to change, but it's most likely how things will go:

  1. Publishing of Version 0.1 alpha of the Civil Voaters' Agreement

    • Complete: Version 0.1 Alpha of the Civil Voaters' Agreement. Requesting feedback so it can be improved.

  2. Solicit feedback from the community

    • /v/Voat: To promote the welfare of the Voat community; to preserve our cultural heritage on Voat; to help newcomers learn useful habits: The Civil Voaters' Agreement
    • /v/AskVoat: If you could create a handbook to Voat for new users, what would you put in it? Please consider checking out this experiment: The Civil Voaters' Agreement

  3. Based on the feeback I (@mumberthrax) will revise it.

  4. Repeat 2&3 until feedback slows down and/or people seem to generally feel ok with it

  5. Release as v0.5 beta, announce that anyone may sign their name to it if they wish

  6. Celebrate!

  7. Invite people to publish their ideas for changes as pull requests or commentary on /v/voatersagreement

  8. Solicit ideas and suggestions for the fine details on the demcoratic review/revision process

  9. 1-2 months after beta, formal democratic review happens, people vote on proposed changes

  10. Version 1.0 is released, announced that anyone may sign their name to it if they wish.

  11. This should begin a regular cycle of 3 or 4 months between CVA review conventions

  12. 3-4 months, invite proposals for changes, alterations, as pull requests or commentary on /v/voatersagreement

  13. Next formal democratic review convention - everyone can vote on changes, or reaffirm support for the agreement as it is

The first draft is basically ready! I'll make a separate post to solicit feedback on it.

I cowered in front of the tall desk belonging to the Human male in the clean blue uniform in front of me. His stern look and uniform remindeFd me of the Hegemony Militia I was on the run from; the uniform, the air of authority and the look of whoever was disturbing him better be worth his time. He sat staring down at me, arms crossed and placed in front of him, mouth tightly closed, an angry slash on his lower face. These race of ‘men’ had been my races enemies for all of my lifetime and I had never been this close to one before. My memory flashed back to the stories of the war – the brutality of man, the speed of their running, vast distances they could walk without stopping, how they would calmly lie on their fronts while under attack and return fire, quickly and accurately without breaking ranks or panic – all without stims! The veterans of the war were horrified at that one, the way they just didn’t lose control when getting attacked like other races did… without emotion, they lay down and shoot apart an ambush attack, talking only to relay commands or report an injury.

Apart from the neatly trimmed bush of hair above his upper lip and overall different - human - shape of the man, I could be back at home about to be interrogated, tortured and ‘disappeared’. It was the uniform. Only the Militia members work a uniform where I come from and going voluntarily to meet one of them was unthinkable. Yet here I was, walking un-escorted into a whole building full of Humans to announce my presence in their territory. In short, I was terrified. It was all I could do to not void my bowels over the floor, all four of my knees trembled.

I had the misfortune to be born on a world occupied and controlled by the Hegemony, one of the victors of the last Galactic war. They weren’t the aggressor, the race that started the war …that would be us. I was only young when the war ended; I have no memory of before the fighting.

The stories are hard to piece together when you are brutally repressed and all information and news comes from Hegemony sources. It seems our planet joined forces with another and attempted to conquer the rest of our galactic area. This sector contained the Humans and the Hegemony. We lost. Towards the end, when those that fought knew the end was coming they tried to surrender to the Humans – we knew the stories of how they treated the defeated. They fed, clothed and healed them, and in return our military did the same for them. I gather our prison conditions were not ideal and transgressions were punished brutally, but most of the humans captured were freed alive after the war.

The Hegemony troops on the other hand did not fare so well, our soldiers slaughtered them as we knew they did to our troops. When we lost they punished all of us for our military’s decisions.

Following the war the Humans and the Hegemony carved up our territories taking control of all our holdings. They were never more than allies of convenience, opposed in almost every ideology, united only against a common foe. Us. Had it not been for us they surely would have been fighting each other – and perhaps still would, some day. Those who were fortunate enough to be able to, scrambled to surrender to the oncoming Humans army. They knew they would be kept alive, humiliated in defeat but alive and given a chance. What was left of my family were not one of the lucky ones. The Hegemony were ruthless, they immediately blockaded the planet with starships, stopping anyone but military personnel coming or going. They forced everyone into re-education camps little better than forced labour and indoctrination facilities. It was here I was introduced to their Militia. Their job was to root out and punish traitors and law breakers. Breaking the law could be as little as speaking badly of any one of them or even being suspected of dissident thoughts. They didn’t need evidence, only a suspicion. Living in Spartan accommodation we had very few options in life; join the Hegemony military, the Militia as a spy or take up a trade in one of the state run education camps. I took a trade and trained as a power repair technician building and maintaining their power supplies. I had access to some restricted machinery, and from that could monitor transmissions.

I saw at first what I knew was propaganda – humans and my race working alongside, in shops, hospitals even going on military patrols and training exercises together! This was the lies the Hegemony told us the Humans would spread. As I saw more and more, families and children of both species playing together in lush parks, tables and shops full of food and clothes with such a wide choice I began to have my doubts. When I saw a transmission of an escaped former colleague of mine waving happily standing next to what looked like a human militia member attending what was called ‘registration’ I knew what I was seeing was the truth. I had to get out.

My escape was a tale of humiliation, discomfort and hunger. I stowed away inside a heating pipe destined for a neutral zone with plenty of civilian traffic, a mining facility operated by a hegemony aligned but independently operated company. That took (3 weeks) of surviving off meagre rations and condensation gathering at the bottom of the box I was in. I’m fortunate that we don’t require much moisture to survive or I no doubt would have died on that trip. I emerged filthy, covered in my own excreta and malnourished, I began the process of finding a ship to take me to human space. Starved and in desperation I simply waited until I saw a human crew member and just told him I requested help. True to his word, he did help. He took me to his captain and form the to his ships small (but functional) infirmary. I do not think they were happy to have me there, some of the crew were obviously old enough to have fought in the war but I was not mistreated. The journey was short – only (12 hours) and they mostly left me alone.

They dropped me off in what they call the ‘village green’ at a pleasant settlement of wooden built houses on one of their colony worlds, a quiet little town with paved roads, blue grass and trees with a small but tidy town centre. It honestly looked like it was from a dream. I had never seen anything beyond my world of hard, cold, plasticrete buildings. Uniformly made in factories and hastily assembled on site, all looking the same. Each house here was clearly made to a similar plan, but each was unique …each a different colour, with various personal transport vehicles outside, different flowers on the grass. It was early morning and the town had not yet woken. I strolled around alone, undisturbed, without being tracked and for the first time in my life, free.

The crew of the human ship had told me I had to report to the local authority to register myself as an immigrant, I would recognise this building by the blue ‘Police’ sign on the outside. I slowly ascended the stone steps, trying to prolong the feeling of freedom and the impending dread. They were sure to take me in for questioning, re-education, probably torture. If I survived the process I might be able to join their society eventually. That’s what the Militia would do, but perhaps the humans would be different - I hoped.

The ‘Policeman’ sat impassively at the desk as I sounded out the well-rehearsed words in my mouth ‘I am an immigrant, I wish to claim political asylum on your planet’

He didn’t move, speak or give any indication he had understood me. I carried on

‘Please. I am hungry and tired. If I go back they will kill me’

The Police man stood up, his chair scraping loudly on the hard floor making me wince in fear. He walked around the desk and stood in front of me, shaking and scared as I was, and held out his right hand, took my hand in his and simply said with a smile that lit his face up;

‘Welcome to New Australia Son’
